title: SREV-012 reparse buffer shape

fsctl_set_shape.description: FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT takes a caller-allocated REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER or REPARSE_GUID_DATA_BUFFER; invalid input returns STATUS_IO_REPARSE_DATA_INVALID

kernel_validator_shape.description: FsRtlValidateReparsePointBuffer is the kernel-only helper; user-mode parsing must not read fields that the helper would reject

name_range_shape.description: Mount-point and symlink tags carry SubstituteNameOffset/PrintNameOffset (byte offsets from byte 0 of PathBuffer) and SubstituteNameLength/PrintNameLength (byte lengths); strings may appear in any order; the documented lengths do not include a trailing Unicode null

tag_specific_overhead.description: Symlink reparse data length covers the path buffer plus 12 bytes after the common header; mount-point reparse data length covers the path buffer plus 8 bytes

range_check_owner.description: File_CheckReparseNameRange validates DataLen >= header, ReparseDataLength <= DataLen-header, PathBufferOffset within header, WCHAR alignment, NameOffset and NameLength within PathBuffer

print_name_copy_invariant.description: Print name copy uses only PrintNameLength bytes from caller and synthesizes the output terminator

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: malformed reparse payloads fail closed; valid symlink and mount-point reparse points still set

contracts: DataLen must cover UFIELD_OFFSET(REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER, GenericReparseBuffer) before tag-specific fields are trusted
ReparseDataLength must fit inside DataLen - header length
PathBufferOffset must lie inside the reparse header and within ReparseDataLength
SubstituteNameOffset/Length and PrintNameOffset/Length must be WCHAR-aligned and fully within PathBuffer
Print name copy must not assume a trailing Unicode null is part of the source payload
